notes.meaning: Micah grieves over how deeply his society has decayed. He compares himself to a hungry worker looking for fruit after the harvest has already finished, finding not a single grape cluster or ripe fig left. True godliness has become just as rare and hard to find among his people.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Scholars disagree about who is speaking in verses 1-6. Some say it is the prophet himself, some say it is Zion (Jerusalem), and some say it is the faithful people of Israel.

notes.meaning: Devout and kind people have disappeared from the land, leaving no one who walks uprightly. Instead of loving their neighbors, people treat each other like prey. They set traps and lie in wait to cheat and harm their own countrymen.

The leaders and judges have grown skilled at doing evil. Rulers demand gifts, and judges decide cases based on bribes rather than justice. Wealthy and powerful people plot together to twist the law to get whatever they want.

Even the best and most respected citizens are like sharp briers that scratch anyone who touches them. God warned the nation through His prophets, who stood as watchmen to announce coming punishment. That day of judgment has arrived, and it will throw the wicked into utter panic and confusion.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: The NET Bible reads the line differently, as "the day you try to avoid by posting watchmen."

notes.meaning: Treachery has spread so widely that no one can trust even a close neighbor or a trusted guide. A person cannot even speak freely to a spouse without fear of betrayal. Selfishness has shattered the most basic human trust.

Family relationships have completely collapsed under the weight of sin. Sons insult their fathers, daughters rebel against mothers, and daughters-in-law oppose their mothers-in-law. A person finds that the fiercest enemies are living under the same roof.

Because no human can be trusted, Micah turns his eyes completely away from people and toward the Lord. He resolves to wait patiently for God to deliver him. He is confident that the Lord will hear his cries and save him.

The faithful people warn their arrogant enemies not to gloat over their downfall. Even though they have fallen and sit in the darkness of affliction, their fall is not final. The Lord Himself will rise to be their light and guide.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Some critics think verses 8 and following were added by a later editor after the exile, though others reject this.

notes.meaning: God's people humbly admit that they have sinned and must accept the Lord's discipline with patience. They know He will eventually step in to plead their case against cruel conquerors. In the end, God will bring them out of the dark and show His saving righteousness.

The mocking enemy who taunted God's people by asking where their God was will be covered with shame. God will vindicate His name by bringing down the oppressor. The proud conqueror will be trampled low like mud in the streets.

A day is coming when the ruined walls of Jerusalem will be rebuilt. When God restores His people, the cruel decrees and limits imposed by foreign empires will be pushed far away. God will broaden the boundaries of His restored community.

differ.view: The promise reaches from the return from exile on to the church that Christ gathers from all nations.
These promises point to a future time when God will restore Israel as a nation.

notes.meaning: People will stream toward God's restored city from vast distances. They will arrive from Assyria, Egypt, the Euphrates River, and distant seas and mountains. God's renewal will draw people together from every direction.

differ.view: The promise reaches from the return from exile on to the church that Christ gathers from all nations.
These promises point to a future time when God will restore Israel as a nation.

notes.meaning: Before that glorious restoration can take place, the land will first become desolate. This ruin comes as a direct consequence of the wicked deeds done by its inhabitants. Judgment must clear away sin before true healing can begin.

Micah prays that the Lord will act as a shepherd and guide His flock with His staff. Though God's people live isolated and surrounded by dangers, the prophet asks God to lead them into rich, fertile pastures like Bashan and Gilead. It is an earnest plea for the Lord to tend and protect His special possession.

The Lord answers the prophet's prayer by promising to display His great power. Just as He did during the Exodus when He rescued Israel from Egypt with mighty miracles, He will show marvelous deeds once again. God's past wonders guarantee that He will rescue His people in the future.

Pagan nations will see what the Lord has done and will be ashamed of their own useless power. They will put their hands over their mouths in silent shock, stripped of all their proud boasting. The Lord's mighty rescue will leave them completely astounded.

Hostile nations will be brought down to the dirt, crawling out of their hiding spots like snakes and worms. They will tremble in terror before the presence of the Lord. Every proud power will bow in dread before Israel's God.

Micah marvels at God's unique nature, asking who could possibly compare to Him. Unlike worthless idols, the Lord forgives sin and overlooks the wrongs done by the surviving remnant of His people. He does not hold onto His anger forever because He genuinely delights in showing loyal love.

differ.view: The "remnant" who receive this pardon are the people God has chosen by His grace.
God's mercy is offered widely, and He is ready to save any sinner who turns back to Him.

notes.meaning: The Lord will turn toward His people with deep tenderness and conquer their sins as if they were defeated enemies. He will throw all their offenses into the deepest parts of the ocean so they are buried forever. When God forgives, He wipes away both the guilt and the dominion of sin.

The prophecy ends with complete confidence that God will keep His promises to Abraham and Jacob. The covenant oaths He made to the ancestors long ago will never be broken. God's unfailing love and truth remain the rock on which His people stand.
